script.title: IEBC Denies Clearing Gachagua, Nairobi Gets AFCON 2027, and More
script.summary: The IEBC clarifies that presidential candidate verification for the 2027 general election has not started. Meanwhile, Nairobi has been named Kenya's sole host city for the AFCON 2027 tournament.
script.intro: The electoral commission has set the record straight on the 2027 presidential election, confirming that former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has not been cleared to run. That clarification headlines this week's review. We also cover Nairobi being named Kenya's sole host city for AFCON 2027, a third labour agreement with Canada, and holiday bus fare increases.

stories.script:
KenGen recorded 713 megawatts of geothermal capacity at Olkaria in Naivasha back in 2022. The plants turn underground steam into steady electricity for homes and businesses across the country. These geothermal facilities generate clean power directly from the earth's heat. That clean power flows straight into our national grid every single day.

This constant supply gives Kenyan homes and enterprises access to clean power from the ground. For ordinary Kenyans, steady electricity keeps daily business running without constant interruptions. KenGen proves that power from the earth's heat can reliably supply our electricity grid. Anyone can visit Naivasha to see where this clean energy rises straight out of the ground.

KenGen reached 713 megawatts of capacity at Olkaria through this underground steam. The clean power from this field remains a cornerstone of Kenya's energy network. The ongoing question is how KenGen will expand this geothermal output to meet national demand.

Nairobi is now confirmed as Kenya's sole host city for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. CAF confirmed this decision on 21 November while reaffirming Kenya's joint hosting alongside Uganda and Tanzania. CAF President Patrice Motsepe declared that the tournament is going nowhere. That statement puts an end to speculation about whether East Africa would actually stage the continental competition.

For local fans, this confirmation means every single AFCON match played in Kenya will take place in Nairobi stadiums. Supporters from across the country will have to travel to the capital to watch the games live. Currently, Kasarani Stadium is undergoing upgrades to meet CAF's strict continental standards. If you plan to buy tickets, stadium delivery is the key factor to monitor.

The Ministry of Sports must publish its stadium completion dates by December. That timetable will show Kenyans whether Kasarani will be fully ready long before ticket sales open. All eyes now turn to the Sports Ministry to see if they meet that December deadline.

On 25 November, the electoral commission dismissed reports claiming it cleared former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua for the 2027 presidential race. The IEBC clarified that verification of presidential candidates has not even started. According to the commission, aspirant verification only begins after formal gazettement takes place. Official candidate nominations cannot happen before those formal legal notices are published.

This statement gives Kenyan voters clarity on the real timeline for candidate clearance ahead of 2027. Speculation had grown around whether the former deputy president would appear on the ballot. Many Kenyans continue to ask whether impeached leaders should be allowed to contest public office in 2027. The commission says no aspirant has received clearance yet because the process remains closed.

The next major milestone comes next month. The IEBC must publish its complete 2027 electoral roadmap by December 2026. Meanwhile, citizens can check their voter status by sending their national ID number to 70000. That official roadmap will finally show when candidate verification actually opens.

Kenya signed a third bilateral labour agreement with Canada on 26 November. The deal expands overseas job opportunities by creating structured pathways abroad for skilled Kenyan workers. The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection signed the pact to help citizens find verified employment. This marks the third formal jobs agreement Kenya has concluded with the Canadian government.

For skilled Kenyans looking for work abroad, this agreement provides structured government access to international employment. Bilateral deals help protect job seekers from unregulated brokers and fake recruitment schemes. The Ministry of Labour stressed that all verified openings under this deal will appear on official government portals. Ordinary Kenyans seeking these foreign jobs are advised to check official Labour Ministry channels directly to avoid scams.

With the framework now signed, job seekers will watch for the official portal listings to open. The true impact depends on how quickly skilled Kenyans can access and secure these verified positions in Canada.

In English football, an FA panel admitted on 26 November that sending off Leny Yoro was an obvious error. The written reasons published by the panel confirmed that the Manchester United defender should not have received a red card against Liverpool. The FA overturned the dismissal after reviewing the incident. Manchester United supporters waited several weeks for the disciplinary body to admit this fault.

Interestingly, referees chief Howard Webb stated that most people saw the original red card as a correct decision. Yet the independent panel came to the exact opposite conclusion in its written findings. Football fans and clubs know all too well how wrong referee decisions can completely distort match results. A single mistaken sending off changes the entire tactical setup and costs teams valuable points on the pitch.

Full details of the written reasons are now public on Sky Sports. For fans watching matches every weekend, the incident keeps the pressure on match officials to avoid obvious mistakes during high-stakes games.

Travelling upcountry just got more expensive after Easy Coach increased fares across its major routes. The bus operator published its new fare chart on its official booking portal on 21 November. The price adjustments affect key long-distance routes across the country right ahead of the December rush. The company advises passengers to check their booking apps before completing any ticket payments.

For everyday travellers, this fare increase pushes up the cost of every cross-country trip. Higher transport fares bite directly into household budgets when families are preparing to travel between towns for the holidays. Moving upcountry is a major end-of-year expense, and higher bus tickets leave less money for other family needs.

With Easy Coach adjusting its rates, passengers will watch whether other long-distance bus operators follow suit. Anyone planning to travel this season must double-check ticket prices on official booking apps before heading to the bus stage.

script.outro: Will you be checking the Labour Ministry portal for jobs in Canada, or are you tracking the stadium upgrades for AFCON 2027 in Nairobi? Share your thoughts in the comments below. Be sure to hit subscribe so you do not miss our breakdown of next week's news on Kenya on Record.
